group_assessment.weighting: The Chang laboratory (Guthrie Research Institute and National Cheng Kung University, from the affiliations) that wrote most of the WOX1 stress-signalling literature. Primary for WWOX/TGF-beta/hyaluronidase signalling in cultured cells; not a Wwox-null, neurological or metabolic group. Observation (blots, counts, images) weighed above the signalling schemes of Figure 10, which the text offers as 'likely' paths.

entries.proposition: The WWOX gain is mouse WOX1 or human WWOX overexpression in L929 and HCT116 cells; the only perturbations of function are a dominant-negative WOX1 and a Hyal-2 antisense construct.
entries.snippet: We selected an antisense construct which allows expression of EGFP and a short stretch of antisense mRNA for Hyal-2, designated EGFP-Hyal-2(as).

experimental_context.genotype: no Wwox allele altered; overexpression of mouse WOX1, Hyal-2 catalytic domain, Smad4; dominant-negative WOX1; Hyal-2 antisense
experimental_context.endpoint: nuclear fractionation blots, FRET, immunogold counts, co-IP, promoter-reporter cell counts

entries.proposition: The evidence that Tyr33 phosphorylation is required for binding Hyal-2 is a yeast substitution (Y33R) and a dominant-negative WOX1 that lowers the complex by about a third in HCT116 cells; phosphorylation itself is not measured in the yeast assay.
entries.snippet: No binding interaction was observed using a phosphorylation mutant, Wox1ww(Y33R), indicating an essential role of Tyr-33 phosphorylation in the binding.
entries.anchor: Results, Hyal-2 Binds WOX1 at the Tyr-33-phosphorylated First WW Domain

entries.proposition: The mitochondrial statement of the Discussion is an inference from earlier papers, not a result of this paper: no mitochondrial fraction or marker is measured here.
entries.snippet: Thus, Hyal-2 and WOX1 are likely to co-translocate, as complexes, to the mitochondria during apoptosis.
